newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Court rejects Air France appeal in CDC case.
newsitem.headline: EU Court rejects Air France appeal in CDC case.

text.p: The European court of justice on Thursday upheld a European Commission decision in 1994 to order the re-payment by Air France of 1.5 billion francs ($288 million) granted by French state-controlled Caisse des Depots et Consignations (CDC).

Air France asked the European Court of First Instance (CFI), the EU's lower court, to overrule the Commission's decision regarding the subscription by CDC in 1993 of nearly the whole of 750 million francs in bonds redeemable into shares and an equal amount of progressive interest subordinatd notes.
"(The court) dismisses the application," the CFI said in its ruling.

The Commission concluded in 1994 that the subscriptions amounted to state aid on the grounds that a reasonable private investor would not have injected that amount of money in Air France in view of its poor financial performance.

Air France contested this. It also argued that, even if the subscriptions involved state aid, the Commission should have left the choice between reimbursement and correction of the subscription terms.

But the court ruled that since the securities had already been subscribed, the Commission did not have to quantify the advantage which Air France gained in relation to market conditions -- which would have called for particularly complex economic appraisals given the nature of the instruments at stake, it said.
The Commission's 1994 decision on the CDC subscription was taken at the same time it cleared a 20-billion-franc rescue package for the troubled French airline.

This second decision was challenged by a certain number of European rival airlines, including British Airways Plc and British Midlands, which argued the conditions put on the aid were not enough to compensate for unfair competition.
